newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Newcrest sees A$550 mln funding task.
newsitem.headline: Newcrest sees A$550 mln funding task.

text.p: Gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Wednesday it faces a funding task of about A$550 million for future projects over the next 18 months and it was considering raising equity, debt and asset sales.

Newcrest chief executive Ian Johnson said the funds would be needed for developments of Cadia project in New South Wales and the Gosowong project in Indonesia, both due to come onstream from around late calendar 1998.

Johnson said this excludes an estimate for the development of the Ridgeway project, near Cadia, which would require about A$150 million to A$200 million capital expenditure. But the funds would include the A$24 million in feasibility work needed on this project.
He said his preferred option was to raise the funds through debt, including management of the company's gold book for profit, but asset sales could come on the agenda.

He named the company's core assets as the Telfer gold mine in Western Australia and the Cadia, Ridgeway and Gossowong desposits -- leaving its shares of the Boddington and New Celebration mines as possible divestment.
"We have not ruled out any of those options," Johnson told reporters.
Newcrest Mining said earlier a review of its Telfer gold mine in Western Australia had delivered a strategy to restore the mine to profitability in 1997/98.
It said the review had demonstrated Telfer had a viable future, but said Newcrest planned to write down the carrying value of the mine by A$100 million pre-tax.
Telfer was forecast to deliver 300,000 ounces of gold in 1997/98 and an average of about 350,000 ounces a year for the three years from 1998/99, it said.
Newcrest shares closed two cents higher at A$3.35 on Wednesday.
